1 This Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is filed by the appellant, challenging the order dated 13.03.2021 passed in M.C.O.P.No.6 of 2018 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Subordinate Judge), Eraniel.

sentences.text:
2.The 2nd respondent filed a claim petition, stating that on 06.01.2017 while he was travelling in the bus belonging to the appellant Transport Corporation, the driver of the Transport Corporation though aware of the noise from the rear tyre, did not stop the vehicle and had proceeded in a rash and negligent manner, which resulted in bursting of the rear tyre, as a result of this, the bottom board of the bus had hit the leg of the claimant, resulting in fracture and other serious injuries to the claimant.
3.The appellant filed counter, stating that the accident did not take place due to the negligence of the driver; that the tyre bursted due to other reasons and it cannot be attributed to the driver; and that in any case, the compensation claimed by the claimant was excessive.
4.On the side of the claimant, he examined himself as P.W.1 and three other witnesses as P.W.2 to P.W.4 and marked 12 documents as Ex.P.1 to P.12.
The appellant has examined R.W.1 driver of the bus.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

5.The Tribunal, after taking into consideration the oral and documentary evidence, held that the accident took place only due to the rash and negligence of the driver of the bus and determined compensation at Rs.5,00,000/- and directed the appellant to pay the compensation to the claimant.

6.The learned counsel appearing for the appellant has submitted that the claimant had not proved his avocation or income and in such circumstances, the notional income fixed by the Tribunal was excessive and the award of the compensation under the head of pain and sufferings was also excessive and hence, prayed for reduction in compensation.
7.The learned counsel appearing for the respondents 3 to 6 has submitted that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable and no interference is called for.

8.The points for consideration in the instant appeal are as follows:-
(a) Whether the Tribunal was right in holding that the accident took place due to the rashness and negligence of the driver of the bus belonging to the appellant Transport Corporation ?; and https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis (b) Whether the compensation is just and reasonable ?.
9.As regards the first point, it is seen that the claimant examined himself as P.W.1.

In his deposition,
he has stated that though there was a noise, the driver of the bus did not stop the bus and had driven the bus in a rash and negligent manner, which resulted in the bursting of the tyre and causing injuries to him.
R.W.1 the driver of the bus has stated that the bursting of the tyre was not due to his fault.
The deposition of R.W.1 is such that it does not inspire confidence.
Ex. P.2

the report of the Motor Vehicle Inspector corroborate the evidence of P.W.1.
10.Considering the facts and circumstances and the evidence on record

, this Court is of the view that the evidence of the claimant is more probable and suggests that the accident took place only due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the bus belonging to the appellant Transport Corporation.
Therefore, the first point is answered accordingly.
11.As regards the quantum of compensation, it is established by the claimant that he was a fisherman.
Though he had claimed that he was earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month, no proof was produced to substantiate the said claim.

Considering the fact that the accident took place in the year 2017 and https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis the claimant has proved his avocation, this Court is of the view that the notional income fixed by the Tribunal at Rs.15,000/- is reasonable.
The Doctor had assessed the disability at 30% and the certificate issued by him was marked as Ex.P.7.

Further,
the award of the compensation under other heads, namely, Transport Expenses,
Extra-Nourishment, Medical Expenses, Pain and Sufferings and Attender Charges are reasonable and hence, deserves to be confirmed.
Therefore, the award of the Tribunal in all aspects is confirmed.

12.The appellant Transport Corporation is directed to deposit the award amount granted by the Tribunal together with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of the claim petition till the date of realization (excluding the period of dismissal for default if any) and costs, less the amount already deposited, if any, within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
13.Since the 2nd respondent / claimant died during the pendency of the appeal, his legal heirs were brought on record as the respondents 3 to 6.
Therefore, the 3rd respondent is entitled to 40 % of the compensation amount and the respondents 4 to 6 are entitled to 20% of the compensation amount together with proportionate interest and costs.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 14.On such a deposit
, the respondents 3 to 6 are permitted to withdraw their respective shares as apportioned supra, less the amount already withdrawn, if any, by filing an appropriate application before the Tribunal.
15.In the result
, this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is dismissed.
No costs.
Consequently, the connected miscellaneous petition is also closed.
